# crashapi

The goal of the crashapi R package is to provide functions for
downloading data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
(NHTSA) [Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
API](https://crashviewer.nhtsa.dot.gov/crashviewer/CrashAPI/).

What is FARS? NHTSA explains: “The Fatality Analysis Reporting System
(FARS) contains data on all vehicle crashes in the United States that
occur on a public roadway and involve a fatality.”

## Installation

You can install the development version of crashapi using the pak
package:

``` r

pak::pkg_install("elipousson/crashapi")
```

## Background

### Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) API support

Supported APIs for this package include:

Get Crash List Information

Get Crash Details

Get Crashes By Location

Get Crashes By Vehicle

Get Summary Counts

Get Variables and Get Variable Attributes

Get FARS Data By Year

Get Crashes By Occupant

Most of these APIs support XML, JSV, CSV, and JSON output formats. This
package only uses JSON with the exception of
[`get_fars_year()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
(which supports downloading CSV files).

For reference, this package also includes a list of terms and NHTSA
technical definitions in `fars_terms` and a list of variable labels in
`fars_vars_labels`.

The FARS API currently provides access to data from 2010 to 2024. The
[NHTSA website](https://www-fars.nhtsa.dot.gov/Help/helplinks.aspx) also
provides additional information on the release data and version status
for the FARS data files available through the API:

| Data Year | File Version | Release Date      |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 2010      | Final        | December 11, 2012 |
| 2011      | Final        | November 13, 2013 |
| 2012      | Final        | December 12, 2013 |
| 2013      | Final        | December 14, 2014 |
| 2014      | Final        | December 18, 2015 |
| 2015      | Final        | December 16, 2016 |
| 2016      | Final        | December 14, 2017 |
| 2017      | Final        | December 18, 2018 |
| 2018      | Final        | June 24, 2021     |
| 2019      | Final        | March 2, 2022     |
| 2020      | Final        | April 3, 2023     |
| 2021      | Final        | April 1, 2024     |
| 2022      | Final        | April 8, 2025     |
| 2023      | Final        | April 1, 2026     |
| 2024      | Annual       | April 1, 2026     |

### Changes to the sex variable

According to the [Data Index terminations
tracker](https://dataindex.us/terminations-tracker), in February 2025
NHTSA renamed the person-level gender variable to “Sex” and recoded its
third response value to “Not Reported”, removing the non-binary category
from published FARS data files. The [FARS 2022 release
notes](https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/2022/FARS2022%20Release%20Notes.txt)
confirm that on February 11, 2025, NHTSA replaced attribute 3 with
attribute 8 (Not Reported), updating 22 records in the PERSON table and
1 record in the PBTYPE table. See [OMB ICR
202503-2127-008](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAViewICR?ref_nbr=202503-2127-008)
and the Williams Institute report [Removal of SOGI from Federal Data
Collections (Feb
2026)](https://williamsinstitute.law.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/Federal-SOGI-Data-Collection-Feb-2026.pdf)
for more information.

Data now returned by the CrashAPI codes `SEX` as 1 (Male), 2 (Female), 8
(Not Reported), or 9 (Reported as Unknown) for all years, so people
previously recorded as non-binary now appear as “Not Reported”.

### Additional data access functionality

The
[`get_fars_zip()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_zip.md)
function can be used to access FARS data files from 1975 to 2024 that
are not available via the API but are available for download through
[the NHTSA File Downloads
site](https://www.nhtsa.gov/file-downloads?p=nhtsa/downloads/FARS/) as
zipped CSV or SAS files. Zipped CSV files are converted to parquet files
and cached in the user cache directory (see
[`tools::R_user_dir()`](https://rdrr.io/r/tools/userdir.html)) so the
data only needs to be downloaded once. This site also provides extensive
technical documentation on coding and use of the FARS data files.

The
[`get_crss_zip()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_crss_zip.md)
function works the same way for data files from the [Crash Report
Sampling
System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/crash-data-systems/crash-report-sampling-system)
(CRSS) from 2016 to 2024. CRSS is a national sample of police-reported
crashes of all severities (not only fatal crashes) that replaced the
General Estimates System (GES) in 2016. Since CRSS is a sample, national
estimates should use the sampling weights and survey design variables
described in the CRSS Analytical User’s Manual, and the data does not
include crash locations.

Earlier data along with data from the [General Estimates
System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/national-automotive-sampling-system-nass/nass-general-estimates-system)
(GES) / [Crash Report Sampling
System](https://www.nhtsa.gov/crash-data-systems/crash-report-sampling-system)
(CRSS) is also available through the [Fatality and Injury Reporting
System Tool](https://cdan.dot.gov/query) (FIRST).

## Examples

``` r

library(crashapi)
library(ggplot2)
```

Use
[`get_fars()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars.md)
to get a FARS data table (e.g. accident, person, or vehicle) for one or
more states, a county, and one or more years. Data for a state from 2010
onwards comes from the CrashAPI and national data or data before 2010
comes from the cached zipped data files.

``` r

# Get the person table for Baltimore City, MD for 2022
md_people <-
  get_fars(
    state = "MD",
    county = "Baltimore city",
    year = 2022,
    type = "person"
  )

head(md_people[, c("ST_CASE", "VEH_NO", "PER_NO", "AGE", "SEXNAME", "INJ_SEVNAME")])
#>     ST_CASE VEH_NO PER_NO AGE SEXNAME            INJ_SEVNAME
#> 133  240061      0      1  58    Male       Fatal Injury (K)
#> 134  240061      1      1  32    Male No Apparent Injury (O)
#> 163  240071      0      1  57    Male       Fatal Injury (K)
#> 164  240071      1      1  37  Female No Apparent Injury (O)
#> 165  240072      0      1  55    Male       Fatal Injury (K)
#> 166  240072      1      1  30    Male No Apparent Injury (O)
```

You can set geometry to TRUE to convert the accident table into an `sf`
object for mapping.

``` r

crashes_sf <-
  get_fars(
    state = "NC",
    county = "Wake County",
    year = 2018:2021,
    geometry = TRUE
  )
#> ℹ Requesting data for all years from 2018 to 2021, including 2019 and 2020 not
#>   in `year`.

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"))
#> Reading layer `nc' from data source 
#>   `/Users/elipousson/Library/R/arm64/4.6/library/sf/shape/nc.shp' 
#>   using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
#> Simple feature collection with 100 features and 14 fields
#> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -84.32385 ymin: 33.88199 xmax: -75.45698 ymax: 36.58965
#> Geodetic CRS:  NAD27
wake_co <- sf::st_transform(nc[nc$NAME == "Wake", ], 4326)

# Map crashes
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = wake_co,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = sf::st_crop(crashes_sf, wake_co),
    aes(color = VE_TOTAL),
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  theme_void()
#> Warning in st_is_longlat(x): bounding box has potentially an invalid value
#> range for longlat data
#> Warning in st_is_longlat(x): bounding box has potentially an invalid value
#> range for longlat data
#> Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
#> all geometries
```

![](reference/figures/README-map_fars_crashes-1.png)

National data or data before 2010 is downloaded and cached the first
time it is used:

``` r

# Get the national vehicle table for 2024
get_fars(year = 2024, type = "vehicle")

# Get the accident table for Maryland for 2005
get_fars(state = "MD", year = 2005)
```

CRSS data files can be downloaded and cached with
[`get_crss_zip()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_crss_zip.md):

``` r

# Get all CRSS tables for 2024
crss_2024 <- get_crss_zip(year = 2024)

# Estimate the number of police-reported crashes using the sampling weight
sum(crss_2024$accident$WEIGHT)
```

Other CrashAPI endpoints are available through specific functions. For
example, you can use
[`get_fars_summary()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
to access state-level summary data on crash and fatality counts.

``` r

# Get summary crash count and fatality count data for Maryland from 2010 to 2021
md_summary <- get_fars_summary(state = "MD", year = 2010:2021)

ggplot(md_summary, aes(x = CaseYear, y = TotalFatalCounts)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_line(color = "red", group = 1) +
  theme_minimal()
```

![](reference/figures/README-get_fars_summary-1.png)

You can list crashes and filter by the number of vehicles involved with
[`get_fars_crash_list()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md).

``` r

# Get fatal crashes in New York state from 2019 with 5 to 10 vehicles
get_fars_crash_list(state = "NY", year = 2019, vehicles = c(5, 10))
#>      CountyName                  CrashDate Fatals Peds Persons St_Case State
#> 1     BRONX (5) /Date(1549865820000-0500)/      2    1       7  360042    36
#> 2     ERIE (29) /Date(1551915000000-0500)/      1    0       4  360159    36
#> 3   QUEENS (81) /Date(1561656240000-0400)/      1    0       6  360319    36
#> 4     BRONX (5) /Date(1561866000000-0400)/      1    0      11  360339    36
#> 5    KINGS (47) /Date(1564564080000-0400)/      1    0       5  360440    36
#> 6 SUFFOLK (103) /Date(1563792360000-0400)/      1    0       2  360551    36
#> 7   ORANGE (71) /Date(1558274040000-0400)/      1    0       1  360277    36
#>   StateName TotalVehicles
#> 1  New York             5
#> 2  New York             5
#> 3  New York             5
#> 4  New York             5
#> 5  New York             5
#> 6  New York             6
#> 7  New York             6
```

If you call
[`get_fars_crashes()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
with details set to TRUE, additional information from
[`get_fars_cases()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
(including the crash date and time) is appended to the crash data frame.

``` r

# Get fatal crashes for Anne Arundel County, MD for 2019 and append details
crashes_detailed <-
  get_fars_crashes(
    state = "MD",
    county = "Anne Arundel County",
    year = 2019,
    details = TRUE
  )

#> ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■          78% | ETA:  3s

dplyr::slice_sample(crashes_detailed, n = 10)

#> 3     24       NA
#> 4     24       NA
#> 5     24       NA
#> 6     24       NA
#> 7     24       NA
#> 8     24       NA
#> 9     24       NA
#> 10    24       NA
```

## Related packages and projects

- [rfars](https://github.com/s87jackson/rfars) aims to “simplify the
  process of analyzing FARS data” by providing access to FARS downloads
  and preprocessed data back to 2015.
- [stats19](https://github.com/ropensci/stats19) “provides functions for
  downloading and formatting road crash data” from “the UK’s official
  road traffic casualty database, STATS19.”
- [njtr1](https://github.com/gavinrozzi/njtr1): “An R interface to New
  Jersey traffic crash data reported on form NJTR-1.”
- [wisdotcrashdatabase](https://github.com/jacciz/wisdotcrashdatabase):
  “A package used for internal WisDOT crash database pulls and
  analysis.”
- [nzcrash](https://github.com/nacnudus/nzcrash): “An R package to
  distribute New Zealand crash data in a convenient form.”
- [GraphHopper Open Traffic
  Collection](https://github.com/graphhopper/open-traffic-collection):
  “Collections of URLs pointing to traffic information portals which
  contain open data or at least data which is free to use.”
- [Open Crash Data
  Index](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rmn6GbHNkfWLLDEEmA87iuy2yHdh7hBybCTZiQJEY0k/edit?usp=sharing):
  A Google Sheet listing a range of city, county, regional and state
  sources for crash data including non-injury crashes as well as the
  fatal crashes available through the FARS API. Contributions for crash
  data from other U.S. cities and states are welcome.

# Package index

## Get data from the FARS API

- [`fars_vars()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/fars_vars.md)
  : Get variables and variable attributes for the Fatality Analysis
  Reporting System (FARS) API
- [`get_crss_zip()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_crss_zip.md)
  : Download CRSS data files as zipped CSV or SAS files
- [`get_fars()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars.md)
  : Get Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) data tables
- [`get_fars_crash_persons()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crash_persons.md)
  : Get Crashes By Occupant
- [`get_fars_crash_vehicles()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crash_vehicles.md)
  : Get Crashes By Vehicle
- [`get_fars_crashes()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
  [`get_fars_cases()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
  [`get_fars_crash_list()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
  [`get_fars_summary()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
  [`get_fars_year()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_crashes.md)
  : Get crash data from the CrashAPI
- [`get_fars_zip()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/get_fars_zip.md)
  : Download FARS data files as zipped CSV or SAS files
- [`read_crashapi()`](https://elipousson.github.io/crashapi/reference/read_crashapi.md)
  : Read data from the CrashAPI using a url template
